intended_object: For a map of finite sets t : S → T, the induced map colim_i Hom(F_i, S) → colim_i Hom(F_i, T), sending [g] to [t ∘ g]. This is the action on morphisms of the functor S ↦ colim_i Hom(F_i, S) (the Hom-functor of the pro-finite-set F). Inferred from the docstring, the name and the lemma stageHomPost_class.
explanation: The body is `(stageHomFunctor F).map t`, where stageHomFunctor F = yoneda ⋙ (whisker by F.op) ⋙ colim. On objects this functor gives colimit (F.op ⋙ yoneda.obj S) = colimit (stageHom F S). On a morphism t it gives the map of colimits induced by the natural transformation "postcompose with t". The library's lemma stageHomPost_class confirms that [g] ↦ [g ≫ t]. This is exactly the intended map, and there are no degenerate-case problems. The construction is generic: it is postcomposition on a colimit of Hom-sets, which would work in any category. Here it is a small component of the library's specific stageHom setup for profinite limits of finite sets, not a narrowed version of an existing Mathlib notion. Mathlib has no named declaration for it; in general form it is just colim.map (whiskerLeft F.op (yoneda.map t)), which is what the body unfolds to.
